candidates.requirement: The database must support a wardrobe recommendation subsystem that keeps track of clothing-item media, wash care history, learned user preferences, item-pair compatibility, outfit performance feedback, and generated style insights. It should reference users, clothing items, and outfits by external identifiers where those parent records live outside this subset, while preserving enough image, care, scoring, feedback, acknowledgement, and update-history information for recommendation and learning workflows.

workload.description: As a user, I want to review my top-performing outfit feedback to understand which outfits work best.
As a user, I want to see my unacknowledged style insights to learn about my wardrobe.
As a user, I want to view the wash history for a specific garment to track its care.

candidates.requirement:
The application must support a rhythm-game competition and community platform that maintains player identity, gameplay history, content metadata, rankings, social activity, and moderation records over time. Player profiles should preserve platform and regional identity, display and avatar settings, performance points, global and country rank, skill breakdowns, lifetime play statistics, profile customization, social links, linked external accounts, mapper identity when applicable, and changes that affect how a player appears or ranks. The platform should retain authentication activity, account-link requests, aliases, bans, badges, achievements with multiple progression levels, prestige rewards, and decorative items awarded or selected by players.

For competitive play, the system should store songs, mapper associations, playable difficulties, gameplay requirements, modifiers, ratings, and leaderboard configuration. Submitted results should capture the player and leaderboard involved, score and accuracy outcomes, performance-point calculations, ranking weight, equipment and pause information, replay location and metadata, improvement history, external status, nominations, redirects, and removal or failure records. Rankings and statistics should be available at player, leaderboard, country, clan, event, and global levels, with enough history to explain significant score, qualification, voting, and rank changes.

Community features should support friendships, favorite maps, custom and featured playlists, mapper catalogs, clans, memberships and managers, clan ranking changes, scheduled events, event participation, and event-specific rankings. Administrative and integration features should include login monitoring, IP and account restrictions, audit records, surveys and support requests, scheduled maintenance data, third-party application registrations, authorization grants and tokens, and configurable game modes, headsets, controllers, and presentation assets. Records that represent requests, votes, nominations, moderation actions, or scheduled publication should retain their status and relevant timing so pending work and historical decisions can be reviewed.

workload.description: Retrieve every achievement that a particular player has earned, including the description and level information for each achievement.
Retrieve a player's basic profile and, if that player is also a mapper, the associated mapper details.
Look up a linked account using an external identifier (such as Steam ID or Oculus ID) to find the associated player.
Find all alias requests that are still awaiting review, with the requesting player and submission time.
Show a player's recent ranked results with song, difficulty, leaderboard, accuracy, performance points, modifiers, equipment, and replay availability, ordered from newest to oldest.
Open a leaderboard for a playable song difficulty and list its highest-ranked results together with player summaries and any active qualification or voting state.
Record a newly verified gameplay result and update the player's aggregate statistics and relevant ranking history while retaining the associated replay information.
Review how a player's latest result improved on an earlier attempt, including changes in score, accuracy, rank, and performance points.
Browse songs created by a particular mapper, including their playable difficulties, gameplay characteristics, ratings, and current leaderboard activity.
Display a clan page with its members and managers, aggregate ranking metrics, recent ranking changes, and any featured playlist.
Add or remove a player from a clan and preserve the membership change needed to recalculate clan standings.
Build a custom playlist for a player or clan by selecting leaderboards and preserving their intended display order.
List participants and leaderboard standings for a scheduled event, including each player's event-specific position and score context.
Review a player's active bans, score removals, name or country restrictions, and the administrative history explaining those actions.
Authorize a registered third-party application for a user, issue time-limited credentials, and later revoke or refresh that access.
Show a player's selected profile presentation, including badges, prestige rewards, avatar or decorative assets, and social links.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a hosting control panel where users manage credits, Discord-linked account information, referrals, server limits, suspensions, and hosted servers. Servers belong to users, are tied to hosting products, and need lifecycle, billing, cancellation, and suspension-warning information. Products describe hosting plans, resource limits, billing periods, pricing, availability, and credit requirements. The platform must handle payments, invoices, coupons, vouchers, partner discounts, referral tracking, ticket support, roles and permissions, application settings, API access, dashboard links, notifications, and activity logging, while preserving timestamps on the main business records where applicable.

workload.description: Verify a discount code is valid at checkout: the code must be active, not expired, still has uses left, and the total amount in the cart meets any minimum required by the code.
Record a completed purchase: store details of the transaction, including the paying user, the amount charged, any discount code used, and the method of payment.
Show all currently running services owned by a user, plus the plan details such as name and price.
Count how many new sign-ups a user has referred, to determine referral bonuses.
Open a new customer support request, including subject, description, urgency level, the user's identity, and the department it belongs to.
Check whether any account is already registered from a given network address, to prevent multiple accounts from the same source.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a small blogging platform where registered users have account credentials, profile details, roles, points, verification state, and timestamps. Blog posts should include authored content, presentation metadata, categories or tags, public URL information, edit history, and view counts. Visitors or users must be able to leave timestamped comments on posts.

workload.description: Find blog posts that contain a search phrase in their title, with the most recent posts shown first.
Find posts that have a tag matching a search phrase, showing the most recent ones first.
Find blog posts by authors whose name includes a search phrase, listed with the most recent first.
Find users whose username includes a given search term.
Show a user's profile by their username, along with their posts from most recent, total number of views on all their posts, and how many comments they have made.
Register a new user account with their chosen username, email, a secured password, profile image, account level, points, registration time, and initial verification status.
After email confirmation, mark the user's account as verified based on their username.
Get a single post using its unique identifier to show its banner image.

candidates.requirement: The database must support managing filament inventory by tracking manufacturers, filament definitions, and individual spools. Manufacturer records should capture identifying details and optional notes or external references. Filament records should describe the material, physical properties such as density and diameter, color information, recommended print settings, pricing or article details, and may be associated with a manufacturer. Spool records should link to a filament and keep inventory details such as measured weights, amount used, first and last use times, storage location, lot information, purchase price, comments, and whether the spool has been archived. The system must also persist application settings as configurable key-value data. Users must be able to attach custom key-value metadata to manufacturers, filaments, and spools without duplicating the same key for the same parent item, while preserving the relationships between spools, filaments, manufacturers, and their custom metadata.

workload.description: Find manufacturers whose name contains a given search term (case-insensitive), sorted alphabetically, returning the first ten results.
Retrieve a specific manufacturer by its unique identifier.
Create a new manufacturer with its name, notes, the weight of an empty spool, and any custom attributes.
Update a manufacturer's name and notes.
Find spools that are not archived, whose filament's material contains a given search phrase, and that are stored at a given location. Return the twenty most recently used spools.
Retrieve a specific spool by its unique identifier, along with its associated filament and manufacturer details.

Create a new spool record specifying the filament it uses, its price, its initial total weight, the weight of the empty spool itself, the storage location, a lot number, notes, and any custom attributes.
Change the storage location of a spool to a new specified location.
Record usage of a spool by reducing its remaining weight by a specified amount and updating the total weight used so far.
Retrieve a list of all distinct filament materials used in the system.
List all storage locations that have at least one spool assigned.
For all spools that are stored in a given location, change their location to a new specified location.
Get the value of a system setting using its unique setting key.
Create or update a system setting with a given key, storing its value and the current time.
Find spools that have a custom attribute with a given name and value (for example, a spool with color attribute set to red).

candidates.requirement: Flagsmith is a feature flag and remote configuration platform that must persist the core tenancy hierarchy of users, organisations, projects, and environments used to manage releases, experiments, and targeting. User accounts store identity, login, profile, marketing consent, and onboarding-related information, and may be associated with external lead-tracking and campaign attribution data. Users can belong to organisations and receive organisation- or environment-level access through permission groups and direct permission records. Organisations own projects, projects contain environments, and environments scope feature evaluations, identities, API access, integrations, and change workflows. Feature flags are defined for projects and can have environment-specific states that record whether the feature is enabled and what value should be served, with optional identity-specific overrides. Identities are scoped to environments and can carry typed traits used for targeting, while segments define reusable targeting rules based on trait keys, operators, and match values, with membership counts tracked per environment. The system must support multivariate feature options and percentage allocations for experiments. Organisation-level master API keys must be stored with names, expiry information, admin capability, creator information, and revocation or deletion state. Changes to features, environments, and related objects must be auditable through history records that capture the actor, time, environment context, and affected object where available. Change requests can be opened for environment changes and can collect user approvals before being committed. Published feature versions must retain environment-specific history with creation, publication, and live timing information. The platform must also persist metadata definitions, imports and exports, release pipeline stages and actions, feature health events, external feature resources, and integrations for code reference scanning and services such as GitHub, GitLab, Slack, webhooks, Datadog, New Relic, analytics, monitoring, and warehouse tools. Analytics data must capture raw feature evaluation and API usage events with environment, feature or resource identifiers, counts, optional identity information, labels, and timestamps, and aggregate those events into time buckets for reporting. The stored data should preserve relationships back to the organisation, project, and environment hierarchy so access control, targeting, auditability, integrations, and usage reporting remain consistent.

workload.description: List all GitHub repositories linked to an organisation's GitHub integration, including repository owner, name, and associated project.
Create a new GitHub repository link for a given GitHub configuration and project, specifying repository owner and name.
Remove a GitHub repository link by its identifier, ensuring it belongs to the given GitHub configuration and organisation.

Retrieve all feature states (enabled/disabled and value) for a given environment, including feature name and multivariate options, used by SDK flag evaluation (default states only, excluding identity-specific overrides).
Store raw feature evaluation events in bulk for analytics processing, preserving the original captured data.

candidates.requirement:
The application must support small-business CRM, project delivery, commercial documents, subscriptions, and accounting within separate workspaces. Each workspace should have its own identity, presentation settings, active state, owning organization when applicable, users and role assignments, document preferences, and a history of users moving between workspaces. People and organizations should share a flexible party model that preserves display and language preferences, billing cycles, registration or tax identifiers, postal addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, roles, groups, memberships, contact relationships, and validity periods for assigned contact details.

Sales and purchasing activity should begin with contracts that identify buyer and supplier parties, responsible staff, preferred currency and document templates, descriptive terms, and purpose-specific contact details. Contracts can lead to quotations, orders, delivery documents, invoices, credit notes, and payment reminders. These documents should preserve their business type and status, issue and due dates, party and staff context, currency, derivation from earlier documents, payment and tracking references, descriptive text, exported media, and line items. Each line item needs a product or service description, quantity, unit, discounts, tax treatment, pricing overrides when permitted, and the latest calculated net and tax values. The catalog should manage product types, individual products, units, currencies, taxes, conversions, prices that vary by unit, currency, customer group, and validity period, and customer-group pricing adjustments.

Project delivery should cover projects, statuses, managers, tasks, task statuses, reporting periods, resources, human-resource assignments, resource managers, and time-dependent resource prices. Staff should record work against a task and reporting period with the date, start and stop times, worked duration, and notes. Planning should also retain resource estimates and agreements for tasks, including applicable periods, amounts, units or costs, and whether an estimate is obsolete or an agreement has been accepted. Projects and tasks may also be connected to other business objects through typed links.

Recurring business should be represented by contract subscriptions, subscription types, renewal and cancellation rules, payment intervals, and dated lifecycle events such as offer, signature, or cancellation. Accounting should support accounts, accounting periods, balanced transfers between source and destination accounts, references back to relevant commercial documents, product-category mappings, and tax account assignments. Reusable document templates, template bundles, standard text sections, user contact assignments, and asynchronous PDF export status should support generation of consistent business documents across these workflows.

workload.description: List all projects belonging to a workspace.
Fetch details of a specific work record, including its linked resource, task, and reporting period.
Add a new task to a project, providing its name, description, and status, and assigning it to the appropriate project and workspace.
Search parties in a workspace by display name, organization identity, contact detail, or business identifier, and return their current roles and primary contact information.
Create an organization and its principal contact, then assign postal, phone, and email details with their purposes and periods of validity.
Open a contract and show its buyer, supplier, responsible staff member, currency, document preferences, and currently valid contact assignments.

Create a quotation or invoice from a contract, including the business parties, dates, currency, template choice, descriptive text, and its relationship to an earlier commercial document when applicable.
Add product or service positions to a commercial document and calculate current prices, discounts, units, and taxes using the applicable catalog and customer-group pricing rules.
List commercial documents in a workspace by document type, status, customer, and due-date range, including their calculated totals and payment references.
Find the price currently applicable to a product for a given customer group, currency, unit, and business date.
List a project's tasks with their current status, completion state, responsible resources, and most recent status-change time.
Record staff time for a task during an open reporting period and later summarize worked hours and resource cost by project, task, and person.
Compare task estimates with accepted resource agreements and actual work for a reporting period, excluding planning records that have become obsolete.
Create a recurring subscription for a contract and append dated offer, signature, renewal, or cancellation events as its lifecycle progresses.
Post a booking within an accounting period that transfers an amount between two accounts and, when relevant, references the commercial document that caused it.
Produce a workspace document using the user's selected template bundle, track the export until completion or failure, and retain the resulting media reference.

candidates.requirement: The database must support organisation-scoped task and Kanban management, allowing each tenant to manage its own boards, columns, members, pipelines, stages, and tasks. Boards contain ordered columns with optional limits and members with roles, while board cards can track titles, descriptions, priority, due dates, completion time, ordering, and optional links to related CRM records such as accounts, contacts, or opportunities. A separate task workflow must support task status, priority, due date, Kanban ordering, custom JSON metadata, and optional links to CRM records such as accounts, leads, opportunities, or cases. Pipelines define ordered stages with colors, type classification, optional status mapping, and optional work-in-progress limits. Records should preserve organisation ownership, creation and update timestamps, and nullable creator/updater references for auditing.

workload.description: List tasks for an organization, optionally filtered by status and priority, showing the most recent activity first.
Retrieve the pipeline that is marked as the default and currently active for the organization, used when creating a new task without an explicit pipeline.
Retrieve all stages for a given pipeline in the correct sequence, including work-in-progress limits and stage classification. This supports the Kanban board display.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a learning platform where users can register, sign in, maintain profile information, receive role-based access, and recover passwords. It should track invitations between users, optional social login details, account activation state, and extended personal or educational profile data. The platform must manage authorization roles and policies, API client access, course enrollment progress, completion status, ratings and feedback, and gamification through badges and achievements tied to user activity. Users should receive notifications with structured content and delivery state, interact with course comments through likes or claps, and the system should maintain supporting reference data such as schools and reusable message templates for notifications or emails.

workload.description: Retrieve a user account matching both an email address and a Facebook identifier.
Count the number of users who were invited by a given account.
Look up an authorization role by its name.
Retrieve API client credentials by their name and secret, including the associated authorization role.
Retrieve active, unread notifications of a general type for a specific user.
Look up a communication template by its name.
Find a badge associated with a given event name and sequence number.
Retrieve a 'first-attempt test' achievement for a user matching a specific event name and test identifier.
Retrieve a course-sharing achievement for a user based on the course and the social media platform used.
Find an achievement linking a user to a specific badge.
Find a fully earned achievement that links a user to a specific badge.
Count the total number of badges earned by a user from completed achievements.
Count how many achievements are linked to a specific badge.
Count achievements associated with a particular event name.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a hosting commerce platform where customers can register, authenticate, manage sessions and API access, and be assigned roles with permission data. The catalog should organize products under hierarchical categories, support configurable product options, pricing plans, multiple currencies, tax rates, coupons, and cart-based checkout with selected plans, quantities, configuration choices, and coupon or currency context. Orders should lead to customer services that represent active or pending product subscriptions, keeping lifecycle status, selected plan and pricing information, quantities, expiration or subscription references, billing agreements, cancellation details, upgrade or downgrade history, and stored configuration selections. Billing must cover invoices, invoice line items, payment transactions, invoice snapshots, customer credit balances, stored billing agreements, and gateway-related payment references. The support system must manage tickets, departments or assignment context, linked services, threaded messages, incoming mail records, and message attachments. Notification capabilities should include reusable templates, delivery preferences, in-app and push notifications, email logs, and push subscription endpoints. The platform must also track OAuth clients and tokens, authentication attempts, audit and debug activity, scheduled job statistics, global or entity-scoped settings, extension registrations, affiliate codes and linked orders, and operational timestamps or soft-deletion state where those concepts apply.

workload.description: Retrieve all subscriptions for the currently logged-in customer, typically displayed on their main subscription overview page.
Show a specific invoice belonging to a user, including its line items and related information, as done in the invoice detail view.
List unread notifications for a user, used to display notification badges or the notification center.
Daily task to identify invoices that are still unpaid and due today for sending reminders, and to find active subscriptions that have reached their end date for suspension.
Admin API endpoint to create a new product under a specific category, requiring verification that the category exists before proceeding.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a lightweight digital loyalty-card wallet where users can register, authenticate, receive a role, and manage their saved cards. Each user should be able to store multiple cards with the barcode or card code details needed for display and scanning, along with presentation information such as name, description, and color, plus simple usage signals like favourites and recent use. Authentication should support long-lived refresh sessions with expiry, revocation, and device context, while password recovery should rely on expiring, revocable codes. The application also needs a small typed settings store and should preserve timestamps for key user, card, and security records.

workload.description: Retrieve all loyalty cards belonging to the currently logged-in user.
Retrieve a specific loyalty card that belongs to the current user.
Add a new loyalty card for the current user.
Update the details of a loyalty card that belongs to the current user.
Remove a loyalty card that belongs to the current user.
Partially update a loyalty card that belongs to the current user.
Register a new account; the first registered user is automatically granted owner privileges.
Retrieve the profile of the currently logged-in user.
Update account details such as display name, email address, or password, ensuring no duplicate email addresses are allowed.
Delete the currently logged-in user's account.
Authenticate with credentials and receive a session token.
Extend an active session by exchanging an existing refresh token for a new one.
End the current session by invalidating the associated refresh token.
Request a password recovery code, subject to rate limiting.
Redeem a password recovery code to set a new password, which also invalidates all existing recovery codes and active sessions.
As an administrator, retrieve the list of all registered accounts.
As an administrator, delete a specific user account, respecting role-based restrictions.
As the owner, change the role assigned to a user.
As an administrator, retrieve all application configuration settings.
As an administrator, update configuration settings with validation of the new values.

candidates.requirement: The application must support a lightweight project management workspace where users can authenticate through local credentials or an external Google identity, manage personal settings, and participate in projects. Projects should support visual and planning metadata, member associations, pinned or timeline-oriented organization, and limited external client access through revocable credentials with usage tracking. Work items can be organized through tickets, statuses, priorities, assignees, and epics, allowing board-style ordering, completion tracking, assignment, and date-based planning. Users should receive structured notifications with read state and contextual data, while project access records, notification records, and personal settings preserve the relationships needed to keep each user's and project's data organized.

workload.description: Retrieve work items for a given project, arranged according to the sequence of their current stage, to display a board-style view.
Mark all unseen alerts as read for a particular account.
Confirm that an external collaborator's credentials are valid and still active.
Look up an existing account using their Google identity during login.
Retrieve all work items assigned to a particular user.
List all participants of a given project.
Get work items with a target completion date falling inside a specified period, for a timeline display.
Mark a single alert as read, ensuring it belongs to the current account.

candidates.requirement: The application must support a personal blog where the owner can publish articles, organize them by authors, categories, and tags, and track basic article metadata such as publication timing, editing mode, status, and view activity. The site should also manage supporting content used by the blog experience, including carousel images, friend links, background music, owner messages, email subscriptions, and visitor profiles. Visitors may be associated with legacy comments and replies, including optional contact, location, and interaction context. The persistent data should preserve relationships between articles and their classifications or tags, keep secondary content available for display, and maintain creation and update history for the main blog records.

workload.description: Group published articles by their publication month and count how many articles exist in each month, to populate a monthly archive navigation on the blog.
Retrieve all published articles associated with a specific tag, to display on the tag detail page.
Retrieve all published articles belonging to a specific category, to display on the category detail page.
Fetch all carousel images sorted by their display priority, for the homepage slideshow.
Fetch all friend links sorted by their display priority, for the friend links page.
Retrieve the list of all email subscriptions, to allow administrators to send emails or export the list.
Retrieve all visitor records, for administrators to manage site visitors.
Fetch all comments sorted by when they were created, most recent first, for administrators to manage comments.

candidates.requirement: The application must support a multi-company accrual accounting platform where each company keeps its own profile, localization, currency setup, members, connected accounts, and financial records. The system should manage chart-of-account structures, bank and connected-bank accounts, contacts such as clients and vendors, offerings, transactions, and journal entries needed for double-entry reporting. It must handle sales and purchasing documents such as invoices, bills, estimates, and recurring invoices, including parties, document status, line items, discounts, taxes, payment progress, recurring schedules, and links between related documents. Users should be able to import and export company data, with progress tracking and failed-row details for imports. The platform must also support notifications, company-scoped budgets with account allocations over time, reusable adjustments such as taxes or discounts, company defaults, document defaults, addresses, departments, and audit-style creator/updater tracking where applicable. The stored relationships and accounting data should allow reports such as balances, aging, payment performance, income, cash flow, and other company-period financial summaries to be produced from the persisted records.

workload.description: Calculate the total values of journal entries for a specific ledger, separated by whether each entry is a debit or credit, and limited to those recorded within a given date range.
For the entity balance summary report, determine the total outstanding amount per client from invoices that have not been settled.
For the aging report, classify invoices per client into aging periods (e.g., current, 1–30 days overdue, 31–60 days), based on the invoice's due date relative to a reference date.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a business application foundation with user accounts, role-based access control, configurable application settings, website content pages, data import and export workflows, notifications, API tokens, sessions, password recovery, caching, and background job processing. Users should have secure login details, activation and deletion lifecycle state, language or permission-related preferences, and access through roles and permissions. Administrators should be able to manage grouped settings, publish or hide website pages with SEO metadata, and track who created content where available. Import and export workflows should record the initiating user, uploaded or generated files, processing progress, completion state, and validation failures for problematic import rows. The platform should also persist personal access tokens, user-facing notifications, session data, queued work, failed jobs, batch processing state, and cache records needed for reliable application operations.

workload.description: Retrieve active user accounts filtered by email domain for management through external applications.
Find all data import jobs completed within a specific month for reporting purposes.
Search website pages by the exact text used in their web address for a global search feature.
List all access rights granted to a particular role.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a multilingual page-based CMS where pages can be organized in a hierarchy, scheduled for publication or expiration, assigned templates or delegation behavior, and optionally redirected to another page or an external URL. Pages should keep lifecycle and modification timing, author information, publication state, and enough tree metadata for ordered navigation. Editors must be able to attach language-specific content blocks to pages, define alternate URLs for pages, associate pages with sites, and manage media assets with titles, descriptions, URLs, file extensions, and creation timing. The stored data should preserve page relationships, aliases, content, media, and site associations needed to render and manage the CMS.

workload.description: Retrieve top-level published pages used for navigation, arranged according to their hierarchical position.
Retrieve all sub-pages that belong under a specific page, preserving the tree structure.
Look up a page alias by its exact web address.
Fetch all content items that belong to a particular category.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a lightweight skin-server backend with user-facing preferences, texture popularity tracking, reporting of inappropriate texture content, notifications, localization text, OAuth-related access metadata, and background job processing. Users should be able to keep basic profile or interface context, while textures can retain engagement signals such as likes. The platform must allow reports to be filed against texture content with reporter, uploader, reason, status, and reporting time so moderation workflows can review them. It should also persist notification data, localized interface text, OAuth scopes or client metadata, and queued jobs needed for application operations.

workload.description: A user files a report on an item by providing the item identifier and a reason. The system checks whether the same user has already reported the same item, reduces a configurable penalty if appropriate, and stores the new report with a pending state.
A user retrieves their own submitted reports, with the most recent entries first, limited to a fixed number per page.

An administrator retrieves all reports, optionally filtered by search terms such as status or text, with results paginated. By default, only pending reports are shown, ordered by the most recent first.

An administrator reviews a specific report and may update its status, or take actions such as removing the reported item or blocking the contributor. The most common action is changing the report's status.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a user-authenticated todo application where registered users can manage their own todo items. User accounts should include the authentication and identity information needed for login, roles, claims, external logins, and security tokens. Todo items should store a title, completion state, and owner relationship so each item can be associated with the user who created or manages it. The stored user, role, and ownership data should support application-level authorization rules such as users managing their own todos and privileged roles performing administrative actions.

workload.description: List all todo items that belong to a specific user.
Retrieve a specific todo item by its identifier, but only if it is owned by the current logged-in user.
Create a new todo item with a title and assign it to the currently authenticated user.
Update the title or completion status of an existing todo item that belongs to the current user.
Delete a todo item that is owned by the current user.
Admin deletes any todo item by its identifier, regardless of ownership.
Register a new user account by providing an email and password.
Authenticate a user by their username to verify their password and generate a session token.

candidates.requirement: The database must support user accounts with profile settings (bio, email visibility, picture), discussions with required public/private status and a default unlocked state, replies that can be marked as best answer, categorization via tags with required descriptions, a points system tracking user engagement with a default starting value, notification storage with read tracking, and configuration flags for enabling or disabling features. It should also record discussion visits with timestamps.

workload.description: Show all discussions that are publicly visible, for the main page or search results.
Log a user's visit to a discussion and update the discussion's visit statistics.
Award points to a user and update their cumulative point balance.
Show notifications that a user has not yet read, displayed on their dashboard.
Check whether a specific configuration setting is turned on.

candidates.requirement: The database must support a small commerce administration area for managing suppliers, tax definitions, and customer vouchers. Suppliers should be identifiable, publishable or active, and associated with a user context. Taxes should keep the rate information and explanatory text needed for pricing or voucher calculations. Vouchers should support unique generated codes, validity periods, active state, fixed or percentage-style value behavior, usage tracking and limits, grouping, optional tax association, and rules for whether voucher values can be combined. The system should also let administrators organize voucher groups and configure how voucher codes are generated.

workload.description: Find a voucher using its generated code to validate it during checkout.
Retrieve all suppliers that are currently active and available for display in the shop.

Find all vouchers that are active and still have remaining uses (either no usage limit set, or the number of times used is less than the limit). This helps identify vouchers that can still be applied to orders.

candidates.requirement: The application is a multilingual CMS for a newcomer guide, managing region-specific content, localization, feature toggles, editors, organizations, feedback, chat, media, and mobile-facing services. Each region can configure which content and platform features are enabled, including events, locations, push notifications, chat, external news, SEO, machine translation, and term explanation support. Editors create regional pages, events, points of interest, imprint content, organizations, media, and push messages, with translations maintained per language and versioned so changes over time can be reviewed. Languages are globally defined, while each region maintains its own active language hierarchy. Pages and language structures support tree organization, events can include schedules or recurrence, and points of interest store address, map, contact, opening-hour, category, and organization information. Users act as editors or administrators with account, profile, organization, security, and interface-preference data. The system also stores chat messages and chat usage summaries, contact information, offer templates, feedback for pages, events, POIs, offers, search results, maps, and regions, and read/review state for staff handling that feedback.

workload.description: Retrieve all regions along with their enabled features and geographic details.
Retrieve a specific region using its unique identifier (slug).
List all active pages for a given region and language.
List all events for a given region and language.
Retrieve the translation of a push notification for a given language.

candidates.requirement: The application must support a full e-commerce platform covering catalog management, customer accounts, carts, orders, fulfillment, payments, accounting, promotions, referrals, notifications, comments, media, and regional tax or shipping data. The catalog should organize products by type, brand, shipping category, variants, inventory, images, properties, and pricing information, while allowing products and variants to become inactive or unavailable over time. Customers should be able to authenticate, maintain addresses, phones, payment profiles, store credit, newsletters, and roles. Shopping and checkout workflows should persist carts, order items, billing and shipping details, coupons, shipments, invoices, payments, returns, and state changes needed to process and track purchases. The platform must also support supplier purchase orders, received inventory, accounting adjustments and ledgers, promotional deals and sales, referral programs, user notifications, comments on business records, product image organization, uploaded media metadata, countries, states, shipping zones, shipping rates, and tax rates with effective timing.

workload.description: Search for products by name, using an alternative method when the primary search service is not available.
List all products for administrative views, with controls to sort and navigate through pages.
View items in a user's current shopping cart during checkout or cart display.
Generate an invoice for a completed order during billing.
Validate a coupon code at checkout by looking up its details and checking expiration.

candidates.requirement: The warehouse management system must support multi-tenant warehouse operations, covering users, roles, menu-based permissions, warehouses, storage areas, goods locations, suppliers, customers, goods owners, product categories, product models, SKU variants, and stock held at specific locations. It should track inbound receiving through advance shipping notices, sorting and put-away quantities, outbound dispatches with picking and fulfillment progress, and detailed stock records including owner, SKU, location, serial, expiry, price, put-away, and freeze state. The system must record operational inventory workflows such as adjustments, movements, freezing or thawing, cycle counts, and stock processing jobs, preserving handlers, quantities, locations, job identifiers, and timing. It should also support configurable approval flows for business documents, document-number generation rules, freight pricing by carrier and route, custom print layouts, and user action logs. Core operational records should remain tenant-scoped and retain creation, update, and validity information where applicable.

workload.description: As a warehouse manager, I want to browse inbound shipment records by filtering on supplier, product details, and the owner of the goods, so I can quickly find specific shipments.
As a warehouse operator, I want to browse outbound delivery records by filtering on customer, warehouse, product information, and a date range, to monitor outgoing shipments.

As an inventory analyst, I want to browse inventory aging data by warehouse, storage location, product details, how long the stock has been sitting, and expiration dates, to spot items that are getting old.

As a mobile user, I want to look up inventory at a particular spot using details like the product, the storage area, the warehouse, and optionally a serial number or expiration date, to quickly check stock on the go.
As an administrator, I want to be able to search across any type of record (such as user accounts) using different filter options like exact matches or partial text, so I can find records quickly.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a small CRM for managing customers, contacts, leads, deals, products, and deal line items. Customer records should keep contact information, an optional primary representative, and aggregate sales information. Contacts may be linked to a customer or kept independently. Leads should track potential opportunities, customer association, status, qualification or disqualification timing, reasons, descriptions, and estimated revenue. Deals should represent sales opportunities that may originate from leads or be created directly, with customer links, estimated and actual revenue, status, win or loss timing, and descriptions. Products should be identifiable catalog items with pricing and availability state, and deal line items should connect products to deals with quantity, unit pricing, and total amounts so customer sales totals and pipeline reporting can be maintained.

workload.description: Retrieve opportunities filtered by their stage and the customer they are associated with. For instance, find all opportunities that are at the Prospect stage and belong to a particular customer.
Retrieve sales deals filtered by their stage, the customer, and optionally the originating opportunity. For example, find all deals that are Qualified and belong to a specific customer.
Search for a catalog item by its unique identifier or name. For instance, locate the item with the code 'PROD-123'.
Retrieve all line items for a specific sales deal to show which catalog items are included in that deal.
Update the overall sales amount for a customer when a deal is marked as qualified, ensuring the customer's aggregate sales is recalculated automatically.
Retrieve all contacts associated with a particular customer account to manage or display them.
Assign or change the primary contact person for a customer account.
Create a new customer record through the management interface.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a health-check monitoring service where users have profile settings for reports, limits, timezone, theme, security, account activity, and billing subscription information. Each user may have a single billing subscription with payment identifiers, plan details, invoice preferences, and billing lifecycle dates. Projects organize checks and team membership, with checks storing scheduling rules, timeout and grace behavior, tags, status, ping counts, and recent activity. Pings should retain request metadata for each check, while notification channels and notification attempts track how alerts are delivered and whether errors occurred. The platform should also store credentials, project API keys, system log records, and operational metadata needed to manage monitoring, alerting, and account administration.

workload.description: Look up the billing subscription for a specific user, for instance to display on a billing dashboard or via an API.
Identify subscriptions whose next billing date falls within the next 30 days, for example to send renewal reminders.

candidates.requirement: The application must support an inventory and manufacturing management system with user profiles, API access, permissions, parts, stock, purchasing, builds, suppliers, customers, reporting, plugins, machines, and data import workflows. Users should have profile preferences, dashboard or theme settings, notification state, and controlled access through permission rules. Inventory data should cover parts, categories, supplier parts, price breaks, stock items, stock locations, stock history, attachments, notes, favourites, and bill-of-material information needed for manufacturing. The system should manage purchase orders and received quantities from suppliers, build orders for assembling parts from stock, and company records that may represent suppliers or customers. It should also persist global and per-user settings, plugin and machine configuration, import sessions with row-level validation results and column mappings, and templates or assets used for labels, reports, and printed documents.

workload.description: List all active parts, along with their names and descriptions.
Retrieve all stock items stored in a particular storage area.
Retrieve all active access keys belonging to a specific user.

candidates.requirement: The application must support a dynamic multi-collection backend with authentication, OAuth login, one-time verification flows, configurable email templates, tenant settings, schema-change tracking, background jobs, and caching. Records in different collections should be able to authenticate through expiring session tokens, temporary one-time tokens, and external OAuth providers, while preserving enough context to associate credentials and login links with the correct collection record. Administrators should be able to configure OAuth providers and authentication email content per collection, store locked or editable tenant settings, and track schema modification work for dynamic structures. The platform must also retain operational data for queued jobs, job batches, failed jobs, cache entries, and cache locks so background processing and runtime performance features can be managed reliably.

workload.description: Retrieve all authentication credentials associated with a specific group and item, used when connecting an external login provider or verifying a login.
Retrieve a particular configuration option by its category and label, for example to load storage preferences for a tenant.
Count how many valid one-time login codes remain for a specific item and purpose, used when verifying a temporary login code.
Create a new external login entry when a user connects a social media account.
Modify the content of a configuration option, for example to adjust storage preferences.
Remove outdated cached data to free up storage.
Show all email message designs associated with a group, used when composing automated emails.
Get details of a specific group of queued tasks, used for monitoring background work.

candidates.requirement: The database must support a personal movie tracking application where users maintain accounts, privacy and display preferences, authentication devices, and optional integrations with media services such as Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Kodi, Trakt, and Mastodon. Users can define personal viewing locations and record movie watch history, including the date watched, repeat plays, notes, ordering, and optional location context. The system should also keep country reference data for movie metadata and associate movies with their production countries, while preserving basic creation or update timing for the records that need it.

workload.description: Fetch all countries ordered by their common English name.
Fetch all user accounts with their display name, email address, and administrator status, listed in the order they were created.
Fetch the display names of all users whose account visibility is set to 'internally visible' or higher, sorted alphabetically by name.
Fetch the display names of all users who have recorded watching a particular movie and whose account visibility is at least 'internally visible', sorted alphabetically by name.
Determine the expiry date associated with a session token using the token's unique string.

candidates.requirement: The database must support AI-assisted workflows for a user feedback product. Each project can define feedback categories and configure an AI provider with credentials, endpoint details, a system prompt, and usage alert thresholds. Teams can create reusable AI prompts for generating or enriching feedback fields, and channel-level issue templates can describe which feedback fields should be considered, whether the template is active, and what model settings to use. The system should record AI token usage by project, provider, category, and calendar date so usage can be monitored over time. These AI-related records should keep lifecycle timestamps and allow inactive or removed configurations to be retained for operational history.

workload.description: Set up a new AI connection for a project. Each connection must be unique to its project and includes the AI provider's credentials, a system instruction, and optionally an endpoint address and a usage alert threshold.
Log daily AI resource consumption for a project. This tracks usage for each type of AI operation and each AI provider on a specific calendar day.
Sum up AI resource consumption by activity type and AI provider for a project over a monthly period. This supports dashboard reporting.
Define a new feedback category for a project. Each category's label must be distinct within the project.
Get all categories for a project, sorted by when they were created.
Create a configuration for automating issue creation in a communication channel. This configuration specifies how feedback entries should be condensed to produce issue suggestions.
Update the creativity setting of an AI configuration used to generate feedback content. This controls how diverse the AI's output will be.

candidates.requirement: The database must support a browser add-on marketplace where add-ons have stable public identifiers, localized descriptive content, icons, support information, categories, screenshots, compatibility details, ownership by users or teams, and aggregate usage or rating statistics. Add-ons can go through releases with version records, uploaded files, licenses, review metadata, signing and validation results, and scanner findings from external security services. Users can maintain marketplace accounts, submit ratings and written feedback, reply to reviews, report inappropriate content, and organize add-ons into collections, while reviewers need queues, subscriptions, notes, canned responses, approval summaries, scoring history, and flags for cases that require extra attention. The platform should also manage homepage and discovery content, featured collections, activity logs, abuse-handling workflows with external moderation integration, administrative configuration, blocked identifiers or names, API access, email/logging records, and historical download or update counts. Records should preserve creation and modification history and prevent duplicate public identifiers or repeated user actions where the product requires a single authoritative record.

workload.description: List all tags available in the marketplace.
Retrieve all active main hero display sections.
Fetch a specific rating and its author's information.
Submit a new rating for a specific version of an add-on by a user.
Register a reviewer to receive alerts about a particular add-on.

candidates.requirement: The database must support a lightweight project management and back-office system for freelancers or agencies. It should keep customer and vendor records, bank account details, project-related payments, invoices with itemized billing information, issue records, task lists, user calendar events, comments, file attachments, role assignments, and activity history. Payments should capture the business context, amount, date, direction, description, and the relevant customer or vendor, while invoices should preserve billing dates, totals, discounts, notes, status, creator, and the related project context. Issues and tasks should support day-to-day project work tracking, including ownership, priority or status where applicable, progress, and ordering. Comments, files, calendar entries, and activity logs should provide enough context to attach collaboration history to the relevant business records and retain timestamps for later review.

workload.description: Retrieve payments for a specific business partner, sorted by most recent first.
Generate a daily payment report for a given date, with entries ordered from latest to earliest.
Produce a monthly payment report for a specified year and month, showing total incoming and outgoing amounts per day.
List all active customers alphabetically.
Generate a daily payment report for a range of dates, with entries sorted from newest to oldest.
Calculate the net earnings for a given year by summing all incoming and subtracting outgoing payments.

candidates.requirement:
The database must support a healthcare operations platform used by clinical staff, service accounts, facility administrators, and other authorized users. Accounts should retain identity and contact details, professional classification and qualifications, activation and verification state, authentication and multi-factor settings, preferences, skills or flags, and contextual role assignments. Permissions and roles may apply within different care organizations or facilities, and the system must preserve which users are assigned to each context. Facilities should retain operational and geographic details, verification and active state, service capacity, and internal organizational and location hierarchies, including user assignments and movement of encounters through locations.

Patient records should preserve demographics, contact and emergency details, identifiers, tags, organization associations, care-team access, and audit-oriented history. A visit should connect a patient to a facility and the relevant care organizations, appointment or booking, current location, care team, status, class, urgency, admission period, hospitalization context, tags, and discharge guidance. Clinical documentation created during care should include medication statements, medication requests and administrations, conditions, allergies, observations, diagnostic reports, consents, notes, and structured form responses. These records should retain status, timing, coded or structured clinical content, authorship and update history, and their patient and visit context. Devices should retain identity, manufacturer and lifecycle details, current location or visit, managing organization, and movement or service history.

Operational workflows should include requests for resources between facilities, assignment and approval state, priority, related patient context, and staff comments. Scheduling should represent bookable staff, services, and locations; public or private schedules; recurring availability rules; exceptions; generated slots; and patient bookings with visit reasons and lifecycle status. Facilities may publish healthcare services and organize their physical locations hierarchically.

The platform should also manage questionnaires, reusable value sets, organization or facility scope, captured responses, form submissions, document templates, and generated file or report artifacts with upload and archive state. Patient billing accounts should retain their service period, charge summary, payment totals, balance, and calculation time. Clinical and operational records should consistently preserve creation, modification, soft-deletion, authorship, and extensible metadata where needed for audit, synchronization, and review, while plugin configuration remains addressable by a stable application-level identifier.

workload.description: Identify user accounts without any recorded login activity.
Filter user accounts based on their professional role or category.
Sort patient visits by urgency level, from most urgent to least urgent.
Fetch all diagnostic reports associated with a particular patient, with access restricted based on user role.
Retrieve a single report template using its unique identifier.
Open a patient summary with demographics, identifiers, organization and care-team associations, recent visits, active conditions, allergies, and current medications.
Register a patient visit at a facility, recording its urgency, class, initial status, care organization, attending context, and starting location.
Update a visit as the patient moves between facility locations, preserving the location interval and current location while retaining the earlier movement history.
Record a clinical observation for a patient visit with its code, effective time, performer, value, interpretation, reference information, and author.
Create a medication request for a patient and later record an administration event with occurrence time, performer, dosage, status, and a link back to the request when applicable.
List active conditions and allergies for a patient, including clinical and verification status, onset or occurrence information, severity, and originating visit.
Create and assign a resource request between facilities, then append staff comments and track approval, assignment, priority, and completion status.
Find available appointment slots for a healthcare service, staff member, or facility location during a date range after applying schedules and availability exceptions.
Book a patient into an available slot with a reason for the visit, then update the booking as it is confirmed, cancelled, or associated with a visit.
Publish a questionnaire for selected organizations or facilities and retrieve completed responses and form submissions for a particular patient or visit.
Generate a patient-facing report from a reusable template, track its upload or archive state, and retain who created or archived the resulting artifact.
Review a device's current facility, location, managing organization, and visit assignment together with its movement and service history.
Open a patient's billing account for a service period and review its status, summarized charges, amount paid, outstanding balance, and last calculation time.

candidates.requirement:
The database must support a multilingual educational content portal in which editors publish courses, course sessions, organizations, subject categories, people, blog posts, programs, and navigation entries through a page-oriented content management workflow. Catalog objects should be attached to editorial pages and retain a separate public counterpart when published, allowing draft changes to coexist with the currently visible version. Courses need stable catalog codes, duration and effort information, listing and self-paced settings, and related sessions. Each session should preserve its external learning-platform link, start and end dates, enrollment window, supported languages, synchronization mode, enrollment count, catalog visibility, display mode, and optional course or certificate pricing and offers. Localized session titles and localized licence names or descriptions should be maintained without mixing languages.

Editors should be able to place catalog references and reusable presentation components onto pages. Supported components include course, organization, category, person, program, blog-post, and licence references; organization listings scoped by category; titled sliders with ordered slide content; rich or plain text; styled layout sections; large banners with media; embedded learning tools; sitemap navigation; nested content; and glimpse cards that link to another page or an external destination. Components should preserve their text, variants, layout settings, links, images, and other media needed for rendering. Navigation entries need submenu and color behavior, while sitemap components need a root and depth or navigation filters.

Publication and authorization should preserve enough information to render the public catalog while editors continue working on drafts. User groups may receive a role over a particular page or folder, and the same role should not be assigned repeatedly for one page. Licences and their localized content should be reusable from multiple page components. The resulting design should support browsing catalog entities, assembling pages from heterogeneous components, synchronizing external sessions, and resolving the correct language and publication state for visitors.

workload.description: Synchronize a course session from an external learning platform by providing the required external link and language preferences, along with optional dates for start, end, enrollment opening, and enrollment closing. This creates a new course session entry in the system.
Open a course catalog page with the course's code, duration, effort, listing settings, and all visible sessions ordered by their relevant dates.
Update a course session after synchronization, including enrollment totals, catalog visibility, display mode, supported languages, dates, and current course or certificate offers.
Retrieve the localized title for a course session in the visitor's preferred language, falling back to the available session information when no translation exists.
List organizations associated with a selected subject category and render each organization using the chosen presentation variant.
Publish changes to a course, organization, person, program, blog post, or navigation entry while preserving the editable draft separately from the public version.
Assemble a page section containing text, a slider and its slide items, a banner, and linked cards, retaining each component's presentation settings and media references.
Render a card that may link either to another managed page or to an external destination, together with its title, content, image, and visual variant.
Display reusable licence information in a requested language, including its name, descriptive content, destination link, logo, and page-specific description.
Assign an editorial responsibility to a user group for a page or folder and list the responsibilities currently granted for that content area.
Generate a navigation section from a selected root page using configured depth, root-inclusion, and navigation-visibility settings.
Render an embedded learning tool using its provider settings, secure consumer credentials, sizing behavior, and placement within a managed page.

candidates.requirement: The database must support a self-hosted dashboard where an operator can manage application shortcuts, bookmark collections, bookmark categories, and cached weather information. Application shortcuts should keep their display name, destination URL, icon, description, visibility, pinning, ordering, and timing information. Bookmarks should be grouped under categories and store their display details, URL, optional icon, visibility, ordering, and timestamps. Categories should support display ordering, visibility, and pinning, while weather data should retain the latest available forecast or current-condition details such as temperature, humidity, wind, cloud cover, day/night state, condition text, and update timing.

workload.description: Get all bookmark categories along with the bookmarks inside each, sorted by their display order within the category and overall, for the dashboard.
Get all pinned shortcuts, sorted by their display order, for the quick-access pinned section.
Get the latest weather information to show the current conditions.
Create a new bookmark entry under a specific category, including its display name, link, optional icon, visibility setting, and sorting order.
Change the display name and link of an existing shortcut based on its unique identifier.

candidates.requirement: The database must support a community forum platform with user accounts, extended profiles, external identity links, discussion categories, topics, replies, comments, reactions or follow-style actions, counters, notifications, OAuth applications, personal notes, photos, devices, locations, flexible settings, wiki page history, search indexing, team membership records, and exception reports. Users should keep login, email, authentication state, profile details, sign-in history, and aggregate community activity counts, while profiles can store structured contact, reward, and preference data. Forum topics should belong to users and categories, support team ownership where applicable, preserve body content, reply and like activity, last-reply metadata, moderation state, mentions, and lifecycle timestamps. Replies and comments should keep their authorship, target context, content, state, references to related replies or objects, and soft-deletion timing. The platform should record user actions against different target objects, maintain reusable counters, and deliver notifications that can reference the actor and related forum objects. OAuth applications, grants, access tokens, push devices, SSO identities, photo uploads, notes, location records, wiki page versions, generic settings, and searchable documents should retain the information needed for authentication, integrations, content discovery, moderation, and audit history.

workload.description: Search for topics and comments by performing a full-text search across forum content, highlighting matched portions of the text, and ordering results by relevance.
Search for user accounts by partial match on their username or display name, returning a small set of top results for autocomplete.

candidates.requirement: The application must support a collaborative document platform where users create, organize, share, discuss, and revisit nested documents. User accounts should keep authentication identity, contact names, locale and timezone preferences, first-connection state, administrative flags, device-account status, and activity timestamps. Documents should support hierarchical organization, titles, excerpts, stable paths, creator tracking, duplication history, attachment metadata, and deletion state for both individual pages and affected child pages. Sharing should allow users or team identifiers to receive document roles, invite people by email, request access, mark documents as favorites, and keep privacy-aware traces of documents they have opened. Discussion features should attach threads to documents, track resolution state and resolver information, store structured comments, and allow emoji reactions from users. The platform should also support account reconciliation workflows driven by CSV imports, keeping the involved accounts, confirmation details, processing status, and logs for review.

workload.description: Search for documents whose title matches a given phrase, ignoring case and accent differences.
Filter to show only documents created by the current user.
Show only documents that the current user has marked as a favorite.
Filter to show only documents that the current user has chosen to hide.
Retrieve all documents that were created, updated, or marked as deleted after a specific point in time, for indexing.
Retrieve permission information for a set of document ancestors, to determine which users have access to each document during search indexing.
Fetch identifiers of public documents that the current user has previously viewed and does not own, to restrict search results to those documents.

candidates.requirement: The system must support a video meeting service where users can manage rooms, recordings, file assets, and external application access. User accounts should store authentication identity, contact names, language and timezone preferences, device or staff status, and account timestamps. Rooms should have a stable public identifier, name, access policy, telephony PIN, and configurable room settings, with share/access records assigning roles to users where needed. Recordings should belong to rooms, keep their processing status, worker context, mode, options, and access permissions for users or teams. Uploaded files, such as room background assets, should retain ownership, descriptive metadata, upload readiness, malware-check information, and deletion history. External applications should be registered with credentials, active status, scopes, and allowed email domains so integrations can be controlled over time.

workload.description: Authenticate an external application and generate a secure token by verifying its registered credentials, confirming it is currently active, and ensuring it is permitted to serve the user's email domain.
List rooms that a delegated user is allowed to see, with results paginated, showing only rooms for which the user has been granted access permissions.

Create a new room with secure default settings, such as a restricted access policy, an automatically generated stable identifier, and an optional telephony PIN. Set the delegated user as the room owner.
List files with optional filters: by file type, upload status, whether the file was created by the current user, and whether the file has been marked as deleted.

candidates.requirement: The application must support a media homescreen rotation service that selects Plex collections, records each rotation attempt, remembers selected collection snapshots before they are applied, and tracks collection usage over time. It should maintain collection-level analytics from watch activity, including play and duration metrics, audience counts, collection context, optional rotation context, and extra provider data. Operators should be able to pin collections to different homescreen sections, customize display order, and review synchronization history for external list sources. The system should track missing media discovered while importing lists from services such as Trakt, Letterboxd, MDBList, TMDb, AniList, MyAnimeList, or generic import feeds, keeping enough source, target library, title, episode, and external identifier information to recognize repeated missing items over time. User accounts should support Plex-linked identity details, roles, status, optional local credentials, and login timing. When missing media is automatically requested through an external request service, the database should record the requested title, media identifier, source integration, processing state, errors, and download timing.

workload.description: Retrieve the history of analytics snapshots for all collections or a specific named collection, listing the most recent records first. The number of records returned can be adjusted, with a typical limit of the latest 50.

Retrieve the top performing collections based on total play count, using the latest available analytics snapshot for each collection. Optionally restrict results to a specific media type or only consider snapshots taken after a particular rotation context.
Retrieve all analytics snapshots associated with a specific rotation event, sorted by total play count from highest to lowest.

candidates.requirement: The application must support a backend platform that can operate separate test and live payment environments, manage scheduled HTTP jobs, publish realtime events, and run project-level compute services. For payments, it should store Stripe connection details, synced product and price catalog data, customer records and mappings to application subjects, checkout and customer-portal sessions, payment history, subscriptions with their items, and webhook events for replay, debugging, and synchronization. Payment records should preserve the relevant Stripe identifiers, customer context, amounts, currency, status, timestamps, metadata, raw provider payloads, and errors needed to reconcile activity over time. Scheduled jobs should keep their name, cron timing, request target, method, secure request configuration, activation state, provider job reference, and execution logs. Realtime messaging should support configurable channel patterns with webhook delivery targets and retain published message payloads, sender context, audience counts, and delivery counts. Compute services should be tracked per project with deployment image, port, resource limits, encrypted environment configuration, region, external runtime identifiers, endpoint, lifecycle status, and operational timestamps.

workload.description: Retrieve all currently available product catalog entries for a specified operating environment (e.g., test or live). This is used to display the catalog in the admin interface and during synchronization after a catalog update from the external payment provider.
Retrieve all pricing options associated with a specific product and operating environment. This is used when setting up checkout sessions and showing available price choices for that product.

Find all checkout sessions filtered by operating environment and current status. This supports the admin dashboard for monitoring checkout activity and the event handler for linking incoming payment events to existing sessions.
Create a new checkout session entry whenever a user initiates a checkout flow through the API. This records the session details for tracking and reconciliation.
Fetch payment transaction history for a given customer account and operating environment. This is used to present billing statements and history to the customer or associated subject.

candidates.requirement: The application must support the full workflow of RAG benchmarking experiments, from ingesting source files and documents through retrieval, generation, evaluation, and reporting. It should store source files, document metadata, page-level content, extracted text chunks, image chunks, and relationships between pages and the chunks derived from them. Queries should keep their text, optional LLM-facing variants, ground-truth generation answers, and retrieval-friendly representations such as embeddings or tokenized forms. The system should record relevance judgments that compare queries against text or image evidence, including grouped judgments and graded relevance. Benchmark pipelines should be defined with names and configuration data, and each pipeline run against a query should preserve generated output, token usage, execution time, and run metadata. Evaluation metrics should be reusable across retrieval and generation tasks, with per-query pipeline scores, retrieved text and image evidence, relevance scores, and aggregate summaries by pipeline so experiment results can be analyzed and compared over time.

workload.description: Retrieve an experiment summary record using the unique identifiers of the pipeline and the evaluation metric that together define it.
Get all page records belonging to a given document, sorted in sequential order.
Find queries whose text includes a specified phrase, ignoring differences in letter case.
Get all source files that belong to a particular category, such as raw input or image data.
Get the best-performing pipelines for a given evaluation measure, sorted from highest to lowest score.
Get all evidence associations for a specific query, sorted first by the grouping identifier and then by the sequence within each group.

candidates.requirement: The database must support an AI assistant application that stores user conversations, individual messages, selected response alternatives, and the search-path evidence used by RAG-style answers. Conversations should keep their title, creator, and timing information, while messages should retain sender type, content, send time, and any selected response choice. The system should track available AI models with provider metadata, download status, validity state, and maintenance timestamps. Application settings should preserve runtime performance options, allowed file paths and applications, model-provider scope, tree-structure scheduling preferences, and the API credentials needed for external model access.

workload.description: Retrieve all conversations sorted by most recent update time.
Retrieve messages of a given conversation in chronological order.
Retrieve all available models sorted by their unique identifier.
Retrieve the application settings.
