Save a model, creating it if it does not exist or updating it if it already exists.
Retrieve search path scores for a selected response, ordered from highest score to lowest.
Delete all available models.

candidates.requirement: The database must support a hotel booking workflow where customers and administrators can be recorded with their account credentials and contact details. Guests should be able to submit reservation requests with stay dates, room preferences, guest counts, special requirements, additional requests, and tracking information. Confirmed or pending bookings should retain the related customer context, status, and staff notes, while pricing records should capture the booking date, number of nights, and total charge needed for reservation and billing workflows.

workload.description: Create a record for a new customer with their name, email, password, and phone, and assign them standard (non-administrator) access.
Look up a customer using their email address, for login verification or checking if the account exists.
Fetch a customer's profile using their unique identifier.
List all customer records, for use by an administrator.
Update a customer's name, password, and phone number based on the customer's unique identifier.
Remove a customer record using their unique identifier.
Verify whether a given email address is already registered by a customer.
Check if the given email belongs to an administrator account.
Create a new reservation along with its booking and pricing records in a single transaction.
Update the reservation details including dates, room type, special requests, number of guests, and tracking information, using the reservation's unique identifier.
Remove a booking record along with its associated reservation and pricing, identified by the booking and customer identifiers.
Retrieve all bookings together with their reservation details, for an administrator.
Get all bookings made by a particular customer, along with the reservation details.
Mark a booking as confirmed using its unique identifier.
Cancel a booking using its unique identifier.
Look up an administrator account using their email address for login.
Fetch an administrator's details using their unique identifier.
List all administrator accounts.
Register a new administrator account.

candidates.requirement: The application must support an administrative management backend with users, roles, menus, organizations, posts, messages, audit logs, and internationalized labels. User records should keep login credentials, personal and contact details, avatar, gender/status indicators, ordering information, tags, location details, role, organization and post associations, optional session token, and login activity such as count, last IP, and last login time. Roles and hierarchical menus should drive access control, with permissions connecting roles to menu entries and menus carrying routing, display, metadata, component, and action-label information. Organizations and posts should be organized as trees for workplace structure, with posts scoped to an organization. The system should store announcements or notifications, track which users have read them, and record user operations with request context, parameters, client environment, IP address, and optional geographic information. It should also maintain a hierarchical internationalization dictionary with labels and translations for Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, and Japanese.

workload.description: Verify user login using the provided account credentials.
Retrieve a paginated list of user records, filtering by account name and account status, and including each user's assigned role, organization, and position details.
Get a paginated list of roles, filtered by role name, role code, and a creation date range.
Retrieve the full hierarchy of navigation options, arranged so that parent items can contain child items.
For a given user, list all menus that are accessible to them based on their assigned role.

Retrieve a paginated list of notifications or announcements, filterable by recipient, title, publication status, and time range, and indicate whether each notification has been read by the current user.
Fetch paginated audit logs of user actions, filterable by the user who performed the action, the type of action, and a time range.
Retrieve the organizational hierarchy as a tree, filterable by organization name and organization code.
Assign a set of menu permissions to a role, replacing any previous assignment.

candidates.requirement:
The application must support durable orchestration of distributed workflows. Teams should be able to register reusable task definitions, versioned workflow definitions, and event handlers with their serialized configuration and activation state. Workflow definitions may evolve through multiple versions, while the system can identify the latest version and find definitions by name when resolving subworkflows. Event handlers should describe the event they observe and remain independently enabled or disabled.

At runtime, each workflow execution should retain a stable identity, optional correlation context, serialized state, creation and update times, workflow type, current status, and start time. The system should preserve which definition produced an execution, which tasks belong to it, which task keys have already been scheduled, and whether an execution is still pending. Each task execution should retain its identity, type, task-definition name, status, timing, serialized state, and workflow context. It should also be possible to record in-progress state and append time-ordered execution logs for operational diagnosis. Search-oriented runtime summaries should allow workflows and tasks to be found by status, type, correlation context, start time, or most recent update without reconstructing every result from serialized state.

Task delivery should use named queues whose messages retain identity, payload, delivery time, priority, popped state, delay information, and creation time. Workers should be able to poll within a domain, record recent polling context, claim due work in priority and age order, and avoid scheduling the same logical task twice within one workflow. Event processing should retain a handler, event, execution and message context so retries do not lose the history of an attempted delivery. Distributed operations also require lease-based locks identified by the protected resource and an expiration time. Together, these records should support registering definitions, starting and locating workflow executions, scheduling and delivering tasks, monitoring progress, handling event-driven actions, diagnosing failures, and safely coordinating concurrent workers.

workload.description: Retrieve the definition of a specific workflow, used when the UI expands a subworkflow node.
Retrieve all task execution records associated with a particular workflow, used by the UI to display the execution progress and task details.
Workers fetch tasks that are ready for processing, ordered by importance and age, and only as many as they can handle.
Register a new version of a workflow definition and later retrieve either that exact version or the latest available version by workflow name.
Create or update a reusable task definition and list task definitions needed to validate a workflow before it is started.
Start a workflow execution from a selected definition, preserve its correlation context and initial state, and record the tasks scheduled for that execution.
Find workflow executions by workflow type, status, correlation context, or start-time range, showing the most recently updated executions first.
When a worker completes or fails a task, update its runtime state, append diagnostic log messages, and expose the changed progress through the parent workflow.
Record worker polling activity for a queue and domain so operators can see whether the expected workers are actively requesting work.
Retry delivery of an event-driven action while retaining the handler, event, workflow execution, and message context needed to recognize an earlier attempt.
List active event handlers for a given event and inspect the serialized configuration used to trigger their actions.
Acquire a lease for a protected resource, renew it while work continues, and allow another worker to acquire it after the lease expires.

candidates.requirement: The platform must support a project management workspace with user accounts, external login identities, roles, permissions, projects, epics, tickets, comments, attachments, notifications, time tracking, and configurable settings. Users can own projects or participate in them with assigned roles. Projects should keep their name, description, owner, workflow style, status, ticket prefix, members, and favorites. Epics organize work within projects and may be nested. Tickets should capture title, content, owner, responsible person, project, status, type, priority, ordering, estimate, shareable code, optional epic, comments, attachments, subscribers, and lifecycle history. The system should record ticket relationships, status-change activity, hours logged by users, optional work categories, timesheet entries by date, personal access tokens, pending email changes, background jobs, and notifications needed for collaboration.

workload.description: For the current account, get the total time logged each day over a specified week period.
For the current account, get the total time logged each month over a specified year.
For the current account, get the total time logged for each activity category over a specified year.

Get all epics for a project (optionally verifying that the current account is the project owner or a project member), and also get tickets that are in that project but not attached to any epic, for roadmap visualization.
Given a unique share code, retrieve the ticket corresponding to that code.
Given a validation token, retrieve the user account associated with that token.

candidates.requirement: The application must support a small online store catalog where authenticated users can manage product categories and product listings. Products should keep their category context, image reference, product name, description, selling price, creation and update times, and deletion state. Categories should store their display name, timestamps, and deletion state so catalog groupings can be managed over time. User accounts should retain names, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses, email verification state, password credentials, remember tokens, and timestamps for login and administration workflows. The system should also keep password reset records, personal access tokens, migration state, and failed background job diagnostics needed for routine application operations.

workload.description: Fetch all active product listings along with the name of the group they belong to, showing eight records per page sorted by newest first.
Fetch active product listings that belong to a chosen group, showing the group's name, eight per page, newest first.
Find active product listings whose product name or category matches a search term. Show the category name, eight results per page, sorted by newest first.
Retrieve one product listing by its identifier, including the name of its group.
Admin retrieves product listings, optionally filtered by a keyword, showing five per page newest first, only active items.
Admin retrieves a single product listing by its identifier for modification.
Admin adds a new product listing, specifying its group, an image file, a product name, description, and selling price.
Admin modifies an existing product listing: can change its group, name, description, selling price, and optionally replace the image.
Admin marks a product listing as removed so it no longer appears in active searches.
Admin retrieves all active groups, showing five per page, newest first.
Admin retrieves the details of a specific group for modification.
Admin creates a new group, providing its display name.
Admin modifies the display name of an existing group.
Admin marks a group as removed so it no longer appears in active listings.
Admin updates their own account details: name, email address, phone number, physical address, and password.

candidates.requirement: Canutin is a personal finance application that must store financial accounts, assets, balance history, transactions, categories, settings, event messages, and import records. Accounts should keep their name, institution, account type, balance grouping, closed state, auto-calculation preference, and, where supported, whether they are excluded from net-worth views. Assets should keep their name, optional symbol, asset type, balance grouping, sale state, and, where supported, net-worth exclusion. Balance records should preserve account or asset values over time, with asset balances also able to include quantity and cost information. Transactions should record date, value, description, category, account, pending state, exclusion from analysis, and import timing. Reference data should classify account types, asset types, transaction categories, and category groups. The application should also store configurable settings, user-facing event records with display behavior and status, and imported transaction details linked to accounts and created transactions.

workload.description: Retrieve financial accounts that are not excluded from net worth calculations, together with their most recent recorded balance, to compute the current balance.
Retrieve assets that are not excluded from net worth calculations, along with their most recent recorded balance, to compute the current balance.
Find all transactions that are not excluded from analysis and occur within a specified date range, to calculate monthly cash flow: income, expenses, and surplus.

List transactions with optional filters: matching a keyword in the description, by specific accounts, by specific categories, by excluding or pending status, or by a date range. Sort results by date from newest to oldest. Include the category and account information for each transaction.
For a given set of transactions, mark them as pending.
Delete a set of transactions by their identifiers, also removing any associated import records.
Retrieve the earliest and latest dates among all transactions to set the default date range for the transactions view.
Add a new transaction with its description, associated account, category, date, and amount.

candidates.requirement: The application must support a multi-tenant database design workspace where users collaborate inside organizations on projects, schema files, design sessions, and agent-assisted editing workflows. Users should keep names, email addresses, and optional avatars, while memberships record which users belong to which organizations and when they joined. Invitations should allow members to invite others by email and preserve inviter, organization, token, invitation time, and expiration time. Projects can be connected to GitHub repositories and schema file paths so incoming schemas can be associated with the right source. Design sessions should record their project, organization, creator, name, optional parent session, current schema content, initial snapshot, source path, and Git reference. Schema edits should be stored as ordered change history with enough information to move forward or roll back. Agent state should be persisted through resumable conversation snapshots, binary artifacts, and task outputs, and design sessions may be made publicly shareable.

workload.description: Retrieve the current schema definition and its revision history associated with a specific design session.
Obtain the initial organization record (for setup purposes).
Look up a user's details (name, email, profile picture) using their identifier.
Process an invitation acceptance by adding the user to the organization's membership and removing the invitation record, after verifying the token's validity and expiration.
Set up a new project including its linked GitHub repository, the mapping between them, and the location of the schema file, ensuring all steps succeed together.

candidates.requirement: TaxHacker is a self-hosted AI accounting application where users upload receipts, invoices, or PDFs and use AI-assisted parsing to organize financial transactions. The database should store user accounts with email, name, avatar or business image, email verification state, membership plan, storage limit, and business address details. Users can define categories, projects, custom fields, currencies, settings, and app-specific data to tailor how transactions are classified and extracted. Transactions should preserve extracted accounting information such as merchant, amount, currency, converted amount, type, notes, issue date, recognized text, itemized data, custom-field values, and category or project references. Uploaded files should keep filename, path, MIME type, metadata, review state, cached parse results, and split status. The system should also support progress tracking for long-running parsing, sessions, external provider accounts, verification tokens, and timestamps for audit and workflow continuity.

workload.description: Retrieve financial records for a specific user, optionally filtered by a search term, time period, category, project, and sorted as needed.
Read a progress tracking record for a specific user to provide real-time progress updates.
Look up an active session using its token to verify authentication and retrieve the associated user account.

candidates.requirement: The database must support a local-first codebase intelligence system that indexes source code repositories for semantic search, regex search, and incremental re-indexing. It should persist metadata for indexed source files, including their paths, names, extensions, detected languages, sizes, content hashes, modification times, and indexing timestamps. It should store parsed code chunks with their source file relationship, chunk type, symbol name, code text, byte and line ranges, language, metadata, and timestamps. It should also store vector embeddings for chunks, including the embedding provider, model, dimensionality, vector data, and creation time, so semantic search can compare query embeddings against indexed code. The stored data should support refreshing changed files, removing stale indexed content, tracking schema version state, and querying code by semantic relevance, text pattern, language, file, symbol, or chunk type.

workload.description: Find code chunks that are semantically relevant to a natural-language search query.
Search indexed code content using a regular-expression or text pattern query.
List indexed source files filtered by programming language or by file path.
Retrieve all parsed code chunks for a specific source file, including symbol and line-range context.
Detect that a source file has changed and refresh its stored chunks and embeddings during incremental indexing.
Remove an indexed source file and clean up the code chunks and embeddings associated with it.
Find indexed chunks that match a specific symbol name or chunk type, such as functions or classes.
Check the stored schema version during startup or migration to determine whether database setup work is needed.

candidates.requirement: The system must support AI assistant conversations, background processing, API authentication, and session management. Conversation records should keep the conversation title, optional user ownership, and all exchanged messages, including agent name, role, text content, attachments, tool activity, usage details, metadata, and timestamps. Background processing should retain queued jobs, batch progress, failed job diagnostics, payloads, exceptions, and lifecycle timing so operations can be monitored and retried. API access should be backed by OAuth client registrations, authorization codes, access tokens, refresh tokens, personal access client records, and personal access tokens, preserving ownership, scopes or abilities, revocation state, expiry, and usage timing. User sessions should store the associated user when available, network/client context, serialized session payload, and last activity time.

workload.description: List agent conversations for a specific user, ordered by most recently updated.
Retrieve all messages for a given conversation, optionally filtered by user and ordered by the time they were last modified.
Find access tokens belonging to a specific user, used to validate user tokens.
Find a refresh token that belongs to a given access token, used when refreshing an expired token.
Check that a personal access token is valid by looking it up using its token value, used for API authentication.
Find a failed job by its unique identifier, for diagnosing and retrying it.
Find sessions based on their last activity time, to remove sessions that have expired.
Retrieve jobs from a specific queue, ordered by the time they are scheduled to run, used by the background worker.
